reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of Quantile Super Learning (QSL) lies in its ability to combine multiple quantile estimators into a single optimal predictor via empirical risk minimization. In the discrete variant, it selects the best among K candidate models based on cross-validated performance, ensuring finite-sample oracle efficiency. The continuous extension generalizes this to convex combinations over a finite grid, enabling smooth interpolation between models. For online settings, the algorithm adapts sequentially by selecting the best model at each time step based on cumulative empirical risk. Each primitive maintains theoretical guarantees under i.i.d. assumptions but faces challenges in nonstationary environments such as sports data where structural shifts occur frequently. The key mathematical duality resides in the equivalence between discrete selection and continuous convex optimization within the same framework. Failure modes arise from unverifiable assumptions like bounded outcomes and margin conditions, as well as the absence of stationarity in real-world applications. These limitations necessitate adaptations for GSE’s dynamic, evolving game states.
